content.body:
The highly manueverable Hurricane enjoyed initial combat success in WWII as a pure fighter. When more advanced German fighter designs became operational the hurricane was found to be better suited as a ground attack aircraft as it was then outclassed in the pure air to air role. Always in the shadow of its more glamorous sister (the Supermarine Spitfire), Hurricanes actually shot down twice as many aircraft during the Battle of Britain as the more famous Spitfires did. Its evenly spaced 8 machine gun armament works well for what is basically a light machine gun specification and produces generally better results than the staggered gun spacing to be found on the Mk I Spitfire.
The RAF sent more than a dozen squadrons of Hurricanes along with many other aircraft to try and stop the German advance, but lost almost all of them as France fell the the overwhelming onslaught.
